blocks.text: How much does a website cost in 2026? From webvise's recent offers: launch sites run **€2,500 to €5,000**, brand plus website packages land around **€7,500**, and full-stack platforms start **under €10,000** and reach five figures.
One of those rows has a public case study behind it: the **OHYP** financing platform, live after six weeks.

You have probably asked an agency for a number and heard "it depends." The answer is true and useless on its own. This guide names the four questions the price actually depends on, publishes webvise's range for each engagement shape, and sets both against published Berlin studio rates.

items: **Four engagement shapes set the price:** focused build with fixed scope and fixed price, custom system, ongoing support, and enterprise time and materials.
**Launch and company sites:** recent webvise offers ran €2,500 to €4,900 fixed price, with a three week average to launch.
**Packages:** brand plus website lands around €7,500. A full first year with site, analytics, hosting, AI assistant, and content stays under €10,000.
**Platforms:** focused full-stack builds start under €10,000, and the OHYP financing platform shipped in six weeks. Larger operations platforms reach five figures.
**Market context:** Berlin MVP sprints start at €18,000, and typical product studio builds run €30,000 to €80,000.

blocks.text: If your project is a fixed-scope launch site, [webvise's landing page service](/services/landing-pages) is the engagement built for exactly that: fixed price from €2,500 and about three weeks to launch.
The four questions that decide the price

Every scoping call at webvise sorts the project with the same four questions. Each answer points at one of four engagement shapes, and the shape sets the pricing logic: fixed price or estimated effort.

items: **Is the scope known before the build starts?** A defined page list, content plan, and launch date make a fixed price possible. Open scope gets estimated after discovery.

**Should the website present the business or run part of it?** A presentation site stays in the launch site range. Accounts, data, and workflows turn it into a custom system, and the budget follows the logic instead of the page count.
**Who keeps it alive after launch?** Ongoing support is its own engagement with its own monthly price. The numbers behind that are in [website maintenance costs](/blog/website-maintenance-costs).
**Does the project sit inside a larger organization?** Several stakeholders, existing systems, and moving requirements push the work into enterprise time and materials, billed per sprint.

blocks.text: Those are the four shapes webvise actually sells: focused build, custom system, ongoing support, enterprise time and materials. Every price on this page maps to one of them.

What a tightly scoped platform buys: OHYP
OHYP is the platform build webvise publishes with a name attached. The full-stack financing platform went from kickoff to live in six weeks.

The budget sat at the bottom of the platform range because the first version was tightly scoped. A sharp v1 is the strongest cost lever a client controls, and it weighs more than any single feature decision.

For projects in this class, [webvise's full-stack development service](/services/full-stack-applications) starts with a discovery call and an effort estimate. The full driver list for platform budgets is in [custom web application cost 2026](/blog/custom-web-application-cost-2026).
Why webvise publishes ranges and no price list

webvise.io has no price list, and the position is codified internally. Effort depends on seven variables, and two projects with identical page counts can land in different price classes once those variables differ.

items: **Workflow:** what the system must do end to end
**Users:** how many kinds of people log in and what each may see
**Integrations:** every external tool the build has to talk to
**Data model:** what gets stored, related, and reported
**AI requirements:** whether models run inside the product and at what quality bar
**Review points:** where a human must approve before something goes out
**Support level:** who answers when something breaks in month four

blocks.text: The rule reaches into the site itself. The AI chat on webvise.io is explicitly forbidden from quoting fixed prices, because a quote without discovery is a guess. Every pricing question it receives routes to a scoping conversation instead.
Where these ranges sit in the German market
Berlin gives usable reference points. Typical projects at CODE's product studio run €30,000 to €80,000, and two Berlin studios publish MVP sprints from €18,000.

rows: recent builds, live in about six weeks

blocks.text: The gap has a mechanism and no catch. Over 25 projects have gone through webvise's AI-native pipeline at a three week average to launch, and webvise.io itself is 100% AI-coded via Claude Code. Fewer build hours per project is the whole discount.
If your project is more product than marketing site, the budget behaves differently again. [MVP development cost 2026](/blog/mvp-development-cost-2026) covers that class with its own numbers.

The fastest route to a real number is a short scoping call that answers the four questions above. webvise estimates effort after discovery, quotes fixed prices for fixed scopes, and puts every number in writing. [Book a call](/#contact) to get a range for your project.
